title: What If Cocoa Could No Longer Grow in West Africa?

scenes.text: What if cocoa stopped growing in West Africa? Your chocolate depends on one corner of the planet.
About 70 percent of the world's cacao grows in West Africa, led by Ivory Coast and Ghana.
Cacao trees need steady rain and high humidity. Above about 32 degrees Celsius they suffer water stress and give fewer seeds.
In 2024, warming added at least six extra weeks above that limit across nearly two thirds of cacao areas in the four biggest producers.
Prices hit a 47-year record in early 2024, and global production fell about 14 percent that season.
One study warned over half of West Africa's cocoa countries could be too hot by 2060. A new tree takes about five years to bear pods.
